Implement a second-generation digital keyboard/touch steering controller for Racing26. The current held binary input eventually requests full +/-1 mechanical rack at road speed, which saturates the front tires and makes the M5 plow straight on corner entry. Preserve the physical rack and analog mouse/wheel full authority. Do NOT increase tire grip or add hidden yaw/stability forces.

Design a physically grounded normal-cornering steering envelope derived from vehicle speed and plausible lateral acceleration/curvature (bicycle-model style is acceptable), with full parking/crawl authority and exact left/right symmetry. A normal sustained key hold at roughly 70-120 km/h must not wind toward parking-lot lock. Preserve fast release and correction behavior. Keep changes focused in digital input shaping and its call site/config plumbing.

Read AGENTS.md and PHYSICS_CONVENTIONS.md first. Add deterministic tests for 6/40/70/100/120 km/h, taps, sustained hold, release, symmetry, and analog bypass assumptions. Run test:conventions, test:digital-steering, relevant steering/cornering tests, strict M5 validation, and build. Explain calibration from physics rather than arbitrary percentages.
